Issued at 1157 AM CDT Thu Sep 24 2026

Today through Saturday...

Late-morning water vapor imagery and objective analysis depict 
midlevel ridging across the southern Plains, with an approaching 
shortwave dampening the ridge locally. On the back side of the 
ridge, a ribbon of both gulf moisture and monsoonal moisture are 
pulling up into the region, pushing PWAT values into the 1.70-1.90" 
range (above the 95th percentile of sounding climatology for
mid-September). Ascent associated with this wave, aided by WAA 
and moisture transport, has maintained a band of showers moving 
into the area this morning. Rain will continue to spread east 
through the afternoon and evening (PoPs 80-100%), with a rumble
of thunder possible across southeast NE. Lowering cloud ceilings
through the day will contribute to the already dreary conditions.
High temperatures will only peak in the 60s today.

Additional disturbances emerging from the Desert Southwest will 
maintain periodic shower chances Saturday as WAA and moisture 
transport persists. Shower coverage will fluctuate through Friday 
(PoPs 30-60%) before increasing Friday night into Saturday morning 
(Pops 70-90%), when stronger ascent supports a broader area of rain. 
Limited instability should keep thunder isolated, with the best 
potential for a few rumbles late Friday afternoon and evening. 

Persistent clouds and rainfall will hold highs on Friday in the 60s. 
Saturday's temperatures will hinge on the timing of precipitation 
ending and subsequent clearing. Where pockets of sunshine return 
early enough in the afternoon, highs could reach the mid 70s, with 
western portions of the area having the best opportunity to 
warm a few degrees, otherwise highs will persist in the 60s. 
Rainfall totals through Saturday are generally forecast around 
1.50-2.00 inches. Latest NBM guidance brings a 55-75% 
probability of at least 2.00 across much of the area, with CAM 
guidance showing pockets of totals approaching 3".

Sunday and Beyond...

Brief upper-level ridging will provide a fleeting break from the wet 
pattern Sunday into early Monday, with dry conditions and pockets of 
sunshine helping push highs into the low to mid 70s. Shower and
thunderstorm chance then increase as the ridge pushes off to 
the east and a deepening trough approaches during the start of 
the work week. Strengthening southerly low-level flow ahead of 
the system will replenish Gulf moisture across the Plains. 
Additional moisture associated with the remnant of Hurricane 
Polo may also draw into the region. 

The approaching trough is expected to spin up a surface low over the 
Front Range early Monday before tracking eastward and sweeping an 
associated cold front across the Plains. Shower and thunderstorm 
chances increase later Monday as the front approaches (PoPs 60-80%), 
with PoPs tapering off and lingering into early Wednesday. The front 
will drop high temperatures back into the 60s. Wet antecedent 
conditions, combined with the potential for heavier rainfall if 
moisture exceeds current expectations, could lead to flooding 
concerns. NBM probabilities are currently 50-70% for at least 1 inch 
and 30-45% for at least 2 inches Monday into Wednesday.

Strong to severe thunderstorms will also be possible where 
sufficient instability overlaps favorable wind shear. GEFS- and EPS-
based machine learning guidance continues to indicate a 5-10% 
probability of severe weather Monday into Tuesday. The timing and 
placement of these threats will becomes clearer as guidance comes 
into better agreement. 

Looking ahead, long range guidance diverges on how quick the system 
will pull away to the east, with the majority of GEFS members 
being fairly progressive and pulling the trough east by mid-day 
Wednesday, bringing a return to sunshine and highs back into the
mid 70s. Conversely, EPS guidance stalls the system over the 
central and southern Plains, bringing more prolonged cloud cover
and moisture through the remainder of the work week.
